content:
- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values.
- When sentiment is bearish (negative) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; increase forecast lows and add downward bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 90+), overshooting true price by 5–10% in next 5–7 days; apply smoothing or lagged decay to spikes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85% of recent high, adjust downward by 2–5% for next 10 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a mid-horizon pivot downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply higher sensitivity to sentiment changes in first 5 days.
